chapter_guidelines.content:
The ICD-10-CM provides codes for different types of myocardial 
infarction. Type 1 myocardial infarctions are assigned to codes I21.0-
I21.4. 
 
Type 2 myocardial infarction (myocardial infarction due to demand 
ischemia or secondary to ischemic imbalance) is assigned to code 
I21.A1, Myocardial infarction type 2 with the underlying cause coded 
first, if applicable. Do not assign code I24.89, Other forms of acute 
ischemic heart disease, for the demand ischemia. If a type 2 AMI is 
described as NSTEMI or STEMI, only assign code I21.A1. Codes 
I21.01-I21.4 should only be assigned for type 1 AMIs.  
 
Acute myocardial infarctions type 3, 4a, 4b, 4c and 5 are assigned to 
code I21.A9, Other myocardial infarction type. 
 
 
 
 
 
The "Code also" and "Code first" notes should be followed related to 
 
 
 
 complications, and for coding of postprocedural myocardial infarctions 
 
 
 
 during or following cardiac surgery.
chapter_guidelines.title: Other Types of Myocardial Infarction

chapter_guidelines.content:
infarction (STEMI) and non-
ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) 
The ICD-10-CM codes for type 1 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) 
identify the site, such as anterolateral wall or true posterior wall. 
Subcategories I21.0-I21.2 and code I21.3 are used for type 1 ST 
elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Code I21.4, Non-ST elevation 
(NSTEMI) myocardial infarction, is used for type 1 non-ST elevation 
myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and nontransmural MIs. 
 
If a type 1 NSTEMI evolves to STEMI, assign the STEMI code. If a type 
1 STEMI converts to NSTEMI due to thrombolytic therapy, it is still 
coded as STEMI. 
 
For encounters occurring while the myocardial infarction is equal to, or 
less than, four weeks old, including transfers to another acute setting or a 
postacute setting, and the myocardial infarction meets the definition for 
“other diagnoses” (see Section III, Reporting Additional Diagnoses), 
codes from category I21 may continue to be reported. For encounters 
after the 4-week time frame and the patient is still receiving care related 
to the myocardial infarction, the appropriate aftercare code should be 
assigned, rather than a code from category I21. For old or healed 
myocardial infarctions not requiring further care, code I25.2, Old 
myocardial infarction, may be assigned.

Code I21.9, Acute myocardial infarction, unspecified, is the default for 
unspecified acute myocardial infarction or unspecified type. If only type 
1 STEMI or transmural MI without the site is documented, assign code 
I21.3, ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of unspecified site.

Encounter Summary:
- Chart excerpt documents acute myocardial infarction with a cardiology note stating “NSTEMI.”
- Troponin is reported to have peaked at 4.2.
- No diagnosis code is documented in the chart excerpt.

Documentation Gaps:
1. Gap: MI type/classification is not fully clarified beyond the label “NSTEMI.”
   Why it matters: ICD-10-CM coding differs materially by MI type. Per coding guidance, I21.4 is for type 1 NSTEMI, while type 2 MI is coded to I21.A1 rather than I21.4 even if described as NSTEMI/STEMI.
   Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’. Troponin peaked at 4.2.”
   Minimal clarification needed: Whether the documented NSTEMI represents type 1 MI versus another MI type, if clinically established.

2. Gap: Timing/episode is not established well enough to exclude a subsequent MI code category.
   Why it matters: A subsequent NSTEMI may code to I22.2 rather than I21.4 when clinically applicable.
   Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
   Minimal clarification needed: Whether this is an initial acute NSTEMI or a subsequent MI episode.

3. Gap: There is no explicit coded diagnosis entry in the excerpt.
   Why it matters: Although the diagnosis appears clinically documented, coding accuracy depends on a final, explicit provider diagnosis statement with adequate specificity.
   Evidence quote: “No ICD coding documented in chart.”
   Minimal clarification needed: Final provider diagnosis documentation with MI type/episode specificity.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Clarification of myocardial infarction type
   Reason query is needed: “NSTEMI” is documented, but coding guidance distinguishes type 1 NSTEMI from other MI types.
   Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’. Troponin peaked at 4.2.”
   Non-leading query text: “The record documents acute myocardial infarction and a cardiology note stating ‘NSTEMI,’ with troponin peak 4.2. For documentation specificity, please clarify the type of myocardial infarction for this encounter, if known.”
   Suggested response options:
   - Type 1 NSTEMI
   - Type 2 myocardial infarction
   - Other myocardial infarction type
   - Acute myocardial injury without myocardial infarction
   - Clinically undetermined
   - Other: ______
   Note: Include “acute myocardial injury without myocardial infarction” only if the provider indicates MI is not actually established; otherwise this option may be omitted by local query policy.

2. Topic: Clarification of episode/status as initial vs subsequent MI
   Reason query is needed: Coding may differ if this represents a subsequent NSTEMI.
   Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
   Non-leading query text: “For this documented NSTEMI, please clarify the episode/status of the myocardial infarction for this encounter.”
   Suggested response options:
   - Initial acute NSTEMI
   - Subsequent NSTEMI
   - Unable to determine
   - Other: ______
   Limitation: The excerpt does not provide prior-MI timing details, so this query is only appropriate if the full chart suggests a recent preceding MI.

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Confirm MI type: type 1 vs type 2 vs other MI type.
- Confirm whether diagnosis is NSTEMI vs another AMI category.
- Confirm whether this is an initial acute MI or subsequent MI.
- Ensure final provider diagnosis statement is present in the chart.
- If MI is type 2 or other type, document the underlying cause/associated condition when clinically established.
- Confirm encounter is within the acute MI timeframe if relevant to code selection.

Risk Flags:
- Potential ambiguity: “acute myocardial infarction” and “NSTEMI” support AMI, but the excerpt does not clarify MI type beyond the NSTEMI label.
- Important coding distinction: official guidance states I21.4 is used for type 1 NSTEMI; if the MI is type 2, code I21.A1 is used instead of I21.4.
- Possible overquery risk: There is not enough excerpted evidence to independently support querying for a specific etiology or underlying cause.
- Possible unnecessary query risk: There is no evidence in the excerpt alone of a prior recent MI, so a “subsequent MI” query should only be asked if supported elsewhere in the chart.
